newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gilts slip in light trade, call money firm.
newsitem.headline: Indian gilts slip in light trade, call money firm.

text.p: Indian government securities were down in quiet afternoon trade Monday while call money was firm at 8.75-9.25 percent, dealers said.
They said high call money rates had weakened sentiment and trade was thin.
In latest deals, the 12.59 percent 2004 bond was traded at 106.95 rupees against its weekend close of 107.02. The 10.85 percent 2001 was quoted 100.55/60 against 100.64.
Dealers said the high call money rates were largely lender-driven.
"There has been no significant outflow of funds after last weeek' bond auction," said a dealer. "Rates should have come down to 5.0-6.0 percent by now but lenders are keeping them up."
The Reserve Bank of India auctioned 30 billion rupees of eight-year bonds last Monday and collected payments from successful bidders on Tuesday.
Call money was trading at 4.25-5.0 percent before the auction.
